1520	You can all see the difference. Look, before that, there are short passages from the Kaf HaChaim,
1521	short passages, whereas here
1522	the Rav writes long passages, he expounds at length
1523	on this matter: what is the definition of cooked wine,
1524	which has no problem of yayin nesech. He brings opinions this way
1525	and that way; in a case of need one may be lenient, anything that went through a process
1526	of pasteurization. And so, for example, Mizrachi, in a case of need, if
1527	he is a non-Jew or a Jew who mixed it, and you have no other possibility,
1528	there is no such possibility, you have no choice, a case of need,
1529	in places that are called "cooked," there is no yayin nesech. If possible,
1530	he says to his brother, "I will pour for you, I will pour for you," that way
1531	it comes out without problems. He pours for his brother,
1532	so there is no problem of yayin nesech. This is a sage, and the head must
1533	understand that a person who is in a secular family,
1534	uncles, close relatives, brothers, sisters who are not religious, must
1535	plan ahead how to do this. More than that:
1536	a person comes to his parents' house, they are not careful
1537	about chametz, they are traditional or perhaps not even that,
1538	but for his sake they respect him. They have chametz in the house, beer, all kinds of whiskey and the like. Fine,
1539	they put it in some separate place. He needs
1540	to make something like a partition, take a sticker and write
1541	"chametz" on all those places. Before that
1542	he should come for the bedikat chametz, come to the house and see everything
1543	that needs to be done. It is written explicitly
1544	in the Shulchan Aruch, siman 440: it says one must make
1545	a partition. If a person is with a ger toshav, with a gentile
1546	in his house, and he has chametz, it is permitted to him; he is a ger
1547	toshav, a gentile, it is permitted to him. Even so, he makes
1548	a partition so that he will not come to eat. So
1549	let him make such a partition inside the cabinets, let him seal it well,
1550	the chametz, so that, Heaven forbid, he does not stumble into eating chametz, and lock
1551	everything, the cabinets.
1552	He can also, when he comes to them
1553	for the bedikat chametz, for a visit, to see what is needed,
1554	he can ask his father and mother about all the chametz: "Did you sell the chametz?
1555	Right?" "Well, that's ours." They don't understand what these things
1556	are. Someone who grew up in a secular home, secular teachers
1557	know nothing, ignorant. What
1558	do you say, that it is from the Rabbis? Tell him, "Your chametz, we have sold it."
